rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with `name`/`description` front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement lets a skill link to files for specialized material. It obliges each such link to say when to read the file.

The file has one real Markdown link: `[CI example](../habeas/references/ci.md)` in workflow step 9. It sits in the sentence "Recommend separate successful collection and `habeas coverage-check` steps in project CI, using the Habeas CI example". That ties the link to a situation, which is recommending CI steps in the report. I read that as saying when to read it.

The skill also names other reference files in inline code rather than as links:
- `references/authoring-failures.md`, in step 1: "If it fails, read…".
- `references/distributed-requirements.md`, in "Proposing requirements": "When a convention applies on its own at many sites… read…".
- `references/fixme.md`, in the "Possible bug" item, which applies if the user defers the fix.

Each of these also says when to read it, so they meet the obligation even if they are counted as links.

I found no violations. No link lacks a stated reading condition.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
